questions.question: A train P travelling at a speed of 15 m/s is able to cross a platform of 200 meter length completely in 30 seconds. Approximately how long will it take train P to cross a man who is coming towards the train on his bike at a speed of 27 km/h? [Note: Ignore the length of the bike.]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train P travelling at a speed of 15m/s covers 200m in 30 seconds.

Speed of a man on a bike = 27 km/h.

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the train = x.

Now, According to the question:

Distance = Speed × Time

(200 + x) = 15 × 30

⇒200 + x = 450

⇒x = 250 m

Hence, the length of the train is 250 m.

Now, the speed of a man on the bike is given 27 km/h

= 27 × (5)/(18) m/s

= 7.5 m/s

So, Time taken by train to pass the man is 

= Distance/ Speed (Here distance is the length of the train and speed = relative speed)

= (250)/(15+7.5)

= (250)/(22.5)

= 11.1 seconds

**Hence, The time taken by the train to pass the man is 11.1 seconds.**

questions.question: A 250-metre-long train running at a speed of 100 km/h crosses another train coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 62 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train 1 = 250 metres

Speed of train 1 = 100 km/h

Speed of train 2 = 62 km/h

Time taken to cross = 10 seconds

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of train 1 + Speed of train 2 (since they move in opposite directions)

Distance = Relative speed × Time

Distance = Length of train 1 + Length of train 2

**Calculations:**

Relative speed = 100 + 62 = 162 km/h

⇒ Convert speed to m/s: (162 times 1000)/(3600) = 45 m/s

⇒ Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 45 × 10 = 450 metres

⇒ Length of train 2 = Distance - Length of train 1

⇒ Length of train 2 = 450 - 250 = 200 metres

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Two trains are travelling in the same direction on parallel tracks. Train A is travelling at 30 km/h and Train B is travelling at 60 km/h. If Train A is 400 m long and it takes Train B two minutes to pass Train A, what is the length of Train B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Train A = 30 km/h

Speed of Train B = 60 km/h

Length of Train A = 400 m

Time taken by Train B to pass Train A = 2 minutes

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of Train B - Speed of Train A

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 60 km/h - 30 km/h

Relative speed = 30 km/h

Convert relative speed to m/s:

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

Relative speed = 30 × (5/18) m/s

Relative speed = 25/3 m/s

Time taken = 2 minutes = 2 × 60 seconds = 120 seconds

Distance covered by Train B to pass Train A = Relative speed × Time

⇒ Distance = (25/3) × 120

⇒ Distance = 1000 meters

Length of Train B = Distance - Length of Train A

⇒ Length of Train B = 1000 m - 400 m

⇒ Length of Train B = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. If the length of each train is 150 m and they cross each other in 15 sec, find the speed of each train (in km/hr).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of each train = 150 m

Time taken to cross each other = 15 sec

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = (Sum of the lengths of trains) / Time taken

Speed of each train = Relative Speed / 2

1 m/s = 18/5 km/hr

**Calculation:**

Sum of the lengths of the trains = 150 + 150 = 300 m

Relative Speed = 300 / 15 = 20 m/s

Speed of each train = 20 / 2

⇒ Speed of each train = 10 m/s

Speed in km/hr = 10 × 18/5 

⇒ Speed in km/hr = 36 km/hr

**Speed of each train is 36 km/hr.**

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 44 km/hr and 70 km/hr. The time taken by faster train to cross a man sitting in the slower train is 72 seconds. What will be the length of the faster train?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 44 km/hr and 70 km/hr

**Formula used**

Time = Distance/(Difference of speed)

**Calculation**

Let the speed of the fast train is Sf , and the speed of the slow train is Sₛ.

⇒ (Length of the fast train)/Time = Sf – Sₛ 

⇒ (Length of fast train)/72 = 5/18 × (70 - 44) 

⇒ Length of fast train = 5/18 × 26 × 72 

∴ Length of fast train = 520

questions.question: A 1000 metres long train is running at the speed of 72 km/hr. If it crosses a bridge in 85 seconds, then what is the length of the bridge?
questions.solution:
Given:

Length of train = 1000 m

Speed of train = 72 km/hr

The train crossed the bridge in 85 seconds.

Concept used:

To cross the bridge, the train needs to travel = Length of train + length of the bridge

Speed × Time = Distance

Calculation:

Length of train = 1000 m

Let the length of the bridge be x

Time taken to cross the bridge = 85 sec.

Speed = 72 kmph = (72 × 5)/18 = 20 m/sec.

To cross the bridge, the train needs to travel = Length of train + length of bridge = 1000 + x

Now,

Speed × Time = Distance

20 × 85 = 1000 + x

⇒ x = 1700 – 1000 = 700

∴ Length of the bridge = 700 m.

**The answer is 700 m.**

questions.question: Two trains, 148 m and 152 m long, are running towards each other on parallel lines at 62 km/h and 46km/h, respectively. In what time will they be clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train 1 = 148 m

Length of Train 2 = 152 m

Speed of Train 1 = 62 km/h

Speed of Train 2 = 46 km/h

**Formula used:**

Time = Total Distance / Relative Speed

Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2

Relative Speed (when trains are moving towards each other) = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2

**Calculation:**

Total Distance = 148 + 152 = 300 m

Relative Speed = 62 + 46 = 108 km/h

Convert Relative Speed to m/s:

⇒ 108 × (1000/3600) = 30 m/s

Time = Total Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 300 / 30

⇒ Time = 10 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Two trains of length 110 m and 85 m are moving in the same direction at 12 m/s and 7 m/s. respectively. Find the time (in seconds) taken by the faster train to cross the slower train.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the first train = 110 m.

Length of the second train = 85 m.

Speed of the first train = 12 m/s.

Speed of the second train = 7 m/s.

**Formula Used:**

 Time = (Distance)/(Relative Speed)

**Calculation:**

Total length of both trains = 110 + 85 = 195 m

Relative speed = Speed of the first train - Speed of the second train = 12 - 7 = 5 m/s

⇒ Time taken to cross = 195 / 5

⇒ Time taken = 39 s

**∴ The time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train is 39 seconds.**
